annotations.title: Check that links load, where they redirect and whether #anchors exist

description: Use when the user asks whether links work, or before links, sources or doc URLs go into an answer, README, report, email or code comment (signals: "are these links dead", "check the links in this README", "does this URL exist", "404", "broken link", "where does this redirect", "is this docs page still there"). Fetches each URL live (GET, redirects followed hop by hop) and returns per link a status: ok, redirected (link the final_url), soft_404 (answers 200 but the title says not found, or a deep link lands on the front page), anchor_missing (the #section id is not on the page), broken (404, 410 or other 4xx), server_error (5xx), blocked (401, 403, 429 or a bot challenge: not proof the page is missing), unreachable (DNS, connection or timeout) or invalid. Each result has http_status, every hop, final_url, page title and canonical; for broken pages it lists the closest real pages from the site's own sitemap (suggestions, the top one re-checked). Give urls (up to 15) or text (Markdown, HTML or plain text; its http and https links are extracted, first 15 checked). Example: {"urls":["https://docs.stripe.com/api/charge","https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/a#attributes"]}. Limits: a page can work in a browser and still be blocked here; pages built by JavaScript may hide anchors; one call makes at most 45 requests.

suggest.description: true (default): for broken pages, look up the closest pages in the site's sitemap.xml. false: skip that lookup.

text.description: Markdown, HTML or plain text (a README, an answer, a doc); every http/https link in it is extracted and the first 15 unique ones are checked. Give urls or text, not both.

urls.description: Up to 15 http or https addresses. A #fragment is checked as an anchor on the page. Give urls or text, not both.

name: vouch_check_links
title: Check that links load, where they redirect and whether #anchors exist
